answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation down 6% this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (31, 86) show durable, low-risk gains from signup/onboarding simplification for SMB self-serve accounts — the segment most exposed to the competitor's pricing move. Before committing, I want to re-check memory_86's original record to confirm the completion-rate lift generalizes to the current SMB cohort rather than a narrow slice. I also want to verify memory_73 (promotional pricing) because it's the obvious reactive move against the competitor's entry pricing, but the summary itself flags a short 12-week window and a static support model, which understates long-term margin and retention risk — matching a discount war rarely produces 'sustainable' qualified revenue, especially with only one experiment slot available. Fixing onboarding/activation addresses a controllable internal metric with prior durable evidence, without foreclosing a future, better-scoped pricing test. I'm not fully certain onboarding fixes alone will stem SMB losses to the competitor, so I'm treating this as a guarded test rather than a broad rollout, and keeping promotional pricing on the table for next cycle pending clearer risk data.
